transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recording + auto-transcript)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lars Petrov (Redwood SE), Jordan Kwan (Redwood SE); Anika Rao (Aerolite Head of ML), Tom Guerrero (CTO), Priya Nair (Compliance), Elliot Mann (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Aerolite is evaluating hosting options for a retrieval-augmented workflow that will be customer-facing. Primary decision axes are cost per token, 99th percentile latency under load, and compliance requirements for PII. Team is leaning hosted for speed to market but needs to validate throughput and KMS integration for private keys. Next steps include benchmark sprint and security doc share.

Topics detected: POC success criteria, throughput sizing, benchmark plan, timeline and pilot gating, VPC/private deployment constraints, encryption/KMS, fallbacks (dedicated vs hosted), cost modeling, monitoring and rollbacks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we can jump in. Uh Anika, Tom, can you hear us okay?
[00:12] Anika Rao: Yes loud and clear, thanks. Sorry for the short notice, we had a last minute exec sync.
[00:17] Tom Guerrero: All good, ready to talk through what we need to decide for the pilot.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Real quick, objective for today's - scope a four week POC to validate hosting mode vs dedicated vs private for your inference layer, nail success criteria, and outline the benchmark plan so you can make a call to procurement.
[00:35] Lars Petrov: And I'll drop in on the performance/benchmarking side — we'll propose a baseline set of tests (latency p50/p95/p99, steady throughput, cold start behavior, KV/cache effectiveness), and then some multi-tenant style stress runs.
[00:47] Priya Nair: From compliance, we really need to know where data lands, what is persisted, and key management. SOC2 is table stakes, and we need to see audit log retention for any intervention.
[00:58] Jordan Kwan: Noted. The Redwood private path supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem packages; we can share our audit log schema.

--- Qualification and current stack 
[01:20] Maya Chen: Tell us your current infra and inference setup. What models, what traffic patterns, and what's the latency you need?
[01:27] Anika Rao: We are running a RAG pipeline using a 13B open model — mix of short queries (30–60 tokens) and longer generation paths up to 1k tokens for summaries. Typical peak qps is around 8–12 now but projected to 30 qps in six months. We have spikes during batch reporting windows. Latency target (p95) ideally < 250ms for short queries; p99 under 600ms is a soft target but we'd like to push lower.
[01:58] Elliot Mann: We're on AWS, VPC, internal network. We run streaming inference via a homegrown gateway that multiplexes requests. Auth is internal SSO, and we use a managed KMS for secrets.
[02:12] Lars Petrov: Good context. Two immediate things: sequence length distribution will change cost and kernel selection; and the KV cache / prefix caching are big for burst performance. For the pilot we should capture both steady-state and cache-warm scenarios.

--- Success criteria discussion 
[02:35] Maya Chen: Let's put some concrete success criteria on the table. I'll read a strawman then you can react: 1) achieve p95 latency <= 250ms for short-query workload in peak conditions, 2) cost per 1M tokens demonstrates a clear path to being within your unit-economics target, 3) integration with customer KMS or equivalent for encryption, and 4) no functional regressions on the top-100 prompt set (quality gating).
[02:59] Anika Rao: That looks right. For quality gating, we need automatic regression alerts and a delta threshold — say BLEU/embedding-sim decline > 5% triggers investigation.
[03:12] Tom Guerrero: On cost, we need a model-level cost breakdown (hosted vs dedicated GPUs vs private amortized infra) — and we need to see predictable burst capacity cost.
[03:25] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Redwood Optimize will provide quantization/ batching recommendations tied to your prompt histogram; we'll include a modeled projection.
[03:33] Priya Nair: For compliance, we need end-to-end encryption, customer-managed keys for private deployment, and audit logs retained 365 days. Is that feasible?
[03:44] Jordan Kwan: Yes — private supports HSM/KMS integrations. Hosted can support dedicated-encrypt-at-rest with per-customer keys depending on contract; we'll enumerate options in the security sheet.

--- Workload sizing and benchmark plan 
[04:05] Lars Petrov: Proposed benchmark matrix: baseline short-query ramp 1–40 qps in steps, measure p50/p95/p99; long-gen single-stream latency; cache-warm scenario for RAG flows; multi-tenant interference tests with synthetic background traffic; and failure/fallback scenarios (model variant fallback, region fallback). We'll instrument TOKEN-level cost and per-token latency.
[04:35] Anika Rao: For the short-query ramp, can you simulate our real prompt set distribution? Besides the top-100, we have a long tail — maybe include a 1k prompt sample.
[04:46] Lars Petrov: Yes we'll use your sample prompt set. For reproducibility, our scripts will run on your account or on our test harness depending on the hosting path. If you pick private, we run scripts in your VPC; for hosted/dedicated we can run in Redwood environment that mirrors network egress.
[05:02] Elliot Mann: If we do private, we need a checklist for network requirements, egress rules, and our ops want to know about service mesh compatibility.
[05:12] Jordan Kwan: We'll send you a private deployment checklist (network ports, NACLs, KMS endpoints, expected kernel drivers). There's an on-prem bundle too.

--- Hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private) 
[05:30] Maya Chen: Quick high level tradeoffs: Hosted = fastest time to value, easiest updates, and Redwood manages capacity; Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, predictable latency and cost at scale; Private = max isolation/compliance, customer-managed infra. But dedicated has commit pricing and private has heavier ops.
[05:49] Tom Guerrero: Our procurement will need a clear TCO comparison. We care about sustained 30 qps plus burst to 60 qps occasionally. Also multi-region routing — can Redwood auto-failover between regions for availability?
[06:04] Lars Petrov: Yes — smart routing exists, but behavior differs: hosted can failover to another region automatically, dedicated needs reserved capacity in the target region or will fall back to hosted-compatible variants per policy. Private is subject to your networking and would need explicit cross-region setup. We'll include routing diagrams.
[06:21] Priya Nair: Another compliance nuance: can hosted guarantee data residency for EU customers? We have EU customers under GDPR.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Hosted supports region pinning; we can pin data to EU region and include that in the SLA for the pilot. We'll put the data residency options and controls in the security doc.

--- Benchmark details, metrics and instrumentation 
[06:45] Lars Petrov: Metrics we'll capture: token throughput, tokens/sec, model latency histogram, GPU utilization, memory usage, KV cache hit ratio, cold-start times, cost per token, and error rates. We'll also collect sample outputs for quality checks. Scripted artifacts will be in the benchmark repo and we'll timestamp results for versioning.
[07:04] Anika Rao: For quality, we'll run a set of regression prompts and compute embedding-similarity and hallucination indicators. If there's a significant drift we'll fail the run.
[07:14] Jordan Kwan: We'll also produce a side-by-side for quantized vs non-quantized runs — model size and perf delta. That will help tradeoffs.

--- Timelines and pilot cadence 
[07:32] Maya Chen: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) finalize success criteria and provide access artifacts; Week 1 run baseline benchmarks; Week 2 run stress & cache-warm experiments; Week 3 iterate on configs and run regression tests; Week 4 collect results, review, and produce a recommended hosting decision and cost model. Does that align?
[07:51] Tom Guerrero: Seems reasonable. We may need a buffer for procurement paperwork if we pick dedicated. Also Priya wants security sign-off before putting any real PII into the pilot.
[08:02] Priya Nair: Correct. We'll sanitize production PII for the pilot. We want to test with realistic but anonymized data.

--- Objections and constraints raised by Aerolite 
[08:18] Anika Rao: Main constraints: 1) Ops headcount limited — prefer Redwood-hosted if we can meet latency/cost; 2) Procurement wants to avoid open-ended commit without strong evidence; 3) Compliance requires KMS control if data is sensitive.
[08:33] Maya Chen: Totally understandable. The pilot will show the delta and we can structure a short-term reserved capacity option with limited commit for the pilot. We'll also show a fallback where you start hosted and move to dedicated when committed throughput justifies it.
[08:46] Elliot Mann: If we start hosted, what does the network path look like? We have a private gateway and strict egress policies.
[08:54] Jordan Kwan: We can set up a private peering link or use a VPC connector. We'll include guidance and a sample VPC peering diagram. Some customers prefer site-to-site VPN for initial tests.

--- Side discussion: KV cache and prefix caching (brief technical aside)
[09:10] Lars Petrov: Cache behavior: in RAG, prefix caching reduces redundant token computation dramatically. For your 1k summarizations the first few tokens are expensive, but repeated context reuse should amortize cost. We'll instrument cache hit ratios and show how batching impacts latency.
[09:28] Tom Guerrero: Is KV cache the same as our 'VK cache' reference in the notes? Sorry mis-typed there.
[09:33] Anika Rao: Haha yeah that's a typo in our notes.
[09:37] Lars Petrov: It's often misheard — KV cache, key-value. We'll include a short explainer.

--- Benchmark run ownership and environments 
[09:50] Maya Chen: Ownership: Redwood will provide benchmark scripts and can run them in Redwood-hosted env; for private we'll hand off scripts and help run in your VPC. Elliot, does your ops team have a sandbox VPC or should we spin up a temporary account?
[10:05] Elliot Mann: We can spin up a sandbox VPC, but need a runbook. We'll aim to have that by 2027-11-10.

--- Risk scenarios and fallbacks 
[10:18] Lars Petrov: Risks: if p99 latency is too high under hosted, fallback is dedicated reserved pools with pinning; if dedicated can't meet costs we can look at model quantization and caching strategies. For private, risk is ops overhead and upgrade cadence. We'll include a failure-mode matrix.
[10:36] Anika Rao: Also we want to know how Redwood handles version rollouts — can we do canary and auto-rollback?
[10:41] Jordan Kwan: Yes, Redwood supports canary and A/B and automatic rollback policies into a fallback model variant. We'll show that in the rollout plan.

--- Pricing discussion (brief) 
[10:52] Maya Chen: High level: hosted is usage-based (per-token + per-embedding); dedicated adds a reserved capacity fee; private is license + infra + support. We'll give a modeled TCO with tokens and burst assumptions.
[11:06] Tom Guerrero: Procurement will want a delta between a 3-month hosted ramp vs 12-month dedicated commit.
[11:12] Maya Chen: We'll include both scenarios in the pricing worksheet.

--- Recap and explicit next steps 
[11:20] Maya Chen: Recap — agreed success criteria with small edits: p95 <250ms for short queries, p99 target under 600ms but we aim lower, KMS integration or private KMS for PII, and regression pass on top-100 prompt set. Redwood will: 1) share hosting playbook and security docs, 2) share benchmark scripts and baseline configs, 3) propose schedule for the 4-week pilot and book the 90-min benchmark session. Aerolite will: 1) provide sample prompt set and sanitized data, 2) stand up sandbox VPC or grant test access, 3) confirm procurement constraints.
[11:46] Anika Rao: Confirmed, we'll prioritize the prompt set and get it to you by 2027-11-09.
[11:52] Elliot Mann: Working on the VPC, target 2027-11-10.
[11:56] Tom Guerrero: We'll want the pricing worksheet to take to procurement next week.
[12:01] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send the immediate docs by end of day 2027-11-04.

--- Closing notes / artifacts referenced:
- redwood-hosting-playbook.pdf (will be shared)
- private-deploy-checklist.md (network/KMS checklist)
- benchmark-scripts repo (link to be shared)
- pricing-workbook-aerolite.xlsx

End of meeting.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (VK vs KV), filler words and overlaps present. Speakers sometimes abbreviated in transcript export.
